member.name: T:Spillgate.InputMeter
member.summary:
The input meter: counts what a codec takes and guards the source.
It counts the bytes the codec actually consumes, not the bytes fetched, so read-ahead buffers give no free ratio credit (SG-R-RAT-02).
It fetches at most bytes at a time, far below the 64 KiB tolerance.
With MaxInput it never requests more than MaxInput + 1 bytes in total (SG-R-INP-01, SG-R-INP-02). The probe byte (number MaxInput + 1) is shown to the codec, but never together with earlier bytes, so a codec that takes its whole window is not charged for a byte it did not need; showing is looking, only consuming counts, and the layer guard checks that after every codec step.
It turns a misbehaving source into a typed failure and remembers it: a source that throws is , a count outside the buffer is (SG-R-RDR-04), a from a lower layer passes through, cancellation is sticky.
It checks the cancellation token on every fetch (SG-R-API-04) and never reads again after a failure.
Not thread safe (SG-R-RDR-07).

member.name: T:Spillgate.LayerGuard
member.summary: The layer guard: everything the specification demands of one layer. Whatever the codec does, the guard never hands out more than MaxOutput bytes in total (SG-I-01), never turns a limit hit into a clean end (SG-I-02), keeps failing with the same error once one occurred (SG-I-03) and contains the failures of the codec (SG-I-05, SG-R-CDC-08).
